messages.subject: parboot() error: 'lib.loc'
parts:
Dear unmarked experts, 

I am trying to use parametric bootstrapping to assess fit on my occuRN models.  My computer has 8 cores. When I run parboot() with nsim >100 and ncores >1, I get the following error: 

> parboot(BBRNV1S12T4, nsim = 100, ncores = 2) Running parametric bootstrap in parallel on 2 cores. Error in checkForRemoteErrors(lapply(cl, recvResult)) : 2 nodes produced errors; first error: no library trees found in 'lib.loc'

I get the same error when I use the package clusterApply to create a backend, which I found in an 2012 thread in this group:

> cl <- makeCluster(getOption("cl.cores", 2)) > clusterExport(cl, c("BBRNV1S12T6", "fitstats")) > clusterSetRNGStream(cl, 123) > sims <- clusterEvalQ(cl, { + parboot(BBRNV1S12T6, fitstats, nsim=20) + }) Error in checkForRemoteErrors(lapply(cl, recvResult)) : 2 nodes produced errors; first error: no library trees found in 'lib.loc'

The same error occurs when I use mb.gof.test(). I could only find two instances of this error on stack exchange, and neither solutions were relevant. 

Anyone know what's going on here? I have no problem installing or loading packages, so I'm not sure what it means by "no library trees found". 

Thanks in advance!
